# Dev console and workbench {#sec-dev-console}

This chapter describes the development surface. The surface is dev-only. It
ships in no release artefact.

## The dev console

The dev console is a native extension, `aee_dev`. It listens on loopback only.
It runs SQF in a live session, reads a `missionNamespace` variable, dumps a
subsystem, drives a scenario and runs a batch of probes. The extension reaches
SQF through the `ExtensionCallback` mission event handler. SQF answers through
`callExtension`.

### The four-layer gate

The channel exists only when four independent layers hold.

1. Build exclusion. The dev project is a standalone HEMTT project outside
   `addons/`. The main project cannot build it.
2. Addon-load exclusion. The release mod list does not name the dev mod.
3. Run-time gate. The poller starts only when file patching is active, the
   sentinel file exists, and the host is a dev host.
4. No arbitrary code. The command surface is a fixed verb table.

When a layer fails, the channel does not exist. There is no handler, no verb
and no log line. The failure is a silent no-op.

### The verb table

The dispatcher accepts a fixed set of operations: `ping`, `get`, `set`, `dump`,
`dumpall`, `eval`, `callfunc`, `batch`, `scenario`, `probes`, `remote` and
`verbs`. `eval` is the only operation that compiles agent input, and it is
reachable only on a fully gated dev session. `callfunc` runs a function only
when its name is on the `AEE_DEV_FUNCS` whitelist.

The generated contract, with the extension command set, the verb table and the
whitelist, is in
[the dev console contract](../research/dev-console-contract.md).

## The visual workbench

The workbench re-applies a visual change without a relaunch. Four keybinds
register under the `AEE Dev` category.

| Keybind | Action |
|---|---|
| Re-apply visual | Releases each effect scope and re-runs the pipeline. |
| Screenshot | Takes a labelled screenshot and logs the paired state. |
| Dump | Writes the full state dump. |
| Overlay toggle | Shows the state dump in an overlay. |

The re-apply releases the optics, nightvision and thermal scopes through the
core registry, then re-runs the five named apply paths. The screenshot lands in
the profile folder and its paired state line names the file.

## Test batching

One live session runs many probes. Each probe has a run class. A `headless`
probe runs on the dedicated server. A `headless-client` probe needs a
non-dedicated machine. An `interface` probe needs a human interface. The runner
reports `client-unavailable` for a probe the machine cannot carry. It never
reports a client probe as passing from a server-only run.

A console result is evidence. It is not a gate. A fact that must gate also gets
a probe file, and the Docker harness runs the probe.

## The manual ceiling

The visual check is manual. A dedicated server renders nothing, so the console
and the harness cannot assert a rendered verdict. The human eye on a client is
the ceiling. The operator presses a keybind, looks at the result, and confirms
the change. The screenshot is evidence for that manual check. It is not an
automated gate.
